messages:
maya: quick sync — bringing up SignalBench-v1 embeddings. ran baseline eval this morning and noticed odd behavior on short queries (<=6 tokens).

maya: recall@10 down ~5% vs our current prod model on the docs-small holdout. silhouette score also fell from 0.62 -> 0.51 for a few clusters.

alex: can you paste the eval command & config?

maya: sure — this is what I ran:
```
run_eval --model signalbench-v1 --dataset docs-small-holdout --k 10 --batch 512 --metric recall@10,precision@1,silhouette --index faiss_ivf32_cosine
```

ryan: @maya thanks. did you use whitening/length-norm? those change silhouette a lot.

maya: nope, raw vectors straight out of the model. tried both cosine and dot — cosine looked marginally better but still lower than baseline.

samira: any quant steps? int8 conversion anywhere?

maya: not for this run. we do have a quantized artifact from the quant pipeline (int8 perchannel) but I kept training checkpoint float32 for purity.

eval-bot: eval-complete signalbench-v1 docs-small-holdout — recall@10=0.734 | baseline-prod=0.783 | precision@1=0.612 | silhouette=0.51 | sha=abc123

ryan: interesting — recall drop concentrated on short/keyword queries? can you share a small failing sample list?

maya: posting 6 failing queries (short):
- "refund policy"
- "login 2fa"
- "install rpm"
- "price tiers"
- "sso setup"
- "api rate limit"

alex: thanks. quick hypothesis: model may encode stopwords/anchors differently, causing short-query embeddings to be noisier. also check tokenization differences vs baseline.

samira: also check kNN index params — ive seen ivf32 with coarse quantization lose short-query neighbors. try brute-force (flat) on a 10k sample to rule out index artifact.

maya: running flat recall test now on a 10k subset, will post results.

(eval-bot): started brute-force kNN job (10k sample) — job id jb-4472

maya: flat-run results: recall@10=0.738 (still below baseline). so not purely faiss index.

ryan: ok that points to the encoder. can we compare per-dim variance and nearest-neighbor distance distribution vs baseline? short queries likely have smaller norm or collapse.

maya: doing quick stats: mean norm(signalbench)=1.02, std=0.21; baseline mean=1.29, std=0.33. distance to 1st neighbor (median) increased by ~12%.

samira: that looks like collapse. could be a training objective mismatch (e.g., heavier temperature/contrast). Do we have the training config?

maya: training logs show temp=0.07 vs baseline 0.1, batch-size larger (2048), more aggressive dropout. attaching excerpt:
```
contrast_temp: 0.07
batch_size: 2048
embed_dropout: 0.2
learning_rate: 1e-4
```

alex: lower temp -> tighter clusters maybe, but collapse for short queries odd. maybe model overfits frequent patterns and collapses rarer short tokens. try increasing temp to 0.1 and re-eval.

ryan: also try length-normalization at inference (L2 norm) and optional suffix caching. sometimes short queries benefit from norming + prefix cache disabled.

maya: quick ablations scheduled: (1) inference L2 norm, (2) temp=0.1 retrain checkpoint, (3) disable embed_dropout at eval-time, (4) small synthetic augmentation of short queries via paraphrase.

maya: plan to rerun all ablations tomorrow morning and post diffs. tagging @ryan @alex for visibility.

alex: thanks — one more ask: pick 50 short-queries as canonical seed set and run recall/nn stability across runs — useful for regression alerts.

maya: done, created seed file seeds/short_queries_signalbench_v1.txt and added to the eval harness.

eval-bot: queued ablation jobs: jb-4473 (L2), jb-4474 (temp0.1), jb-4475 (dropout0) — will update when done. :spinner:
